sources.name: TeraWulf: Kentucky PSC approves Justified RESA
sources.excerpt:
TeraWulf Inc. (Nasdaq: WULF) (“TeraWulf” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated owner, developer and operator of large-scale digital infrastructure, today announced that the Kentucky Public Service Commission (“PSC”) has approved the Retail Electric Service Agreement (“RESA”) supporting up to 482 megawatts (“MW”) of electric service for TeraWulf’s Justified Data Campus in Hancock County, Kentucky. The approval represents an important milestone for Justified and, in TeraWulf’s view, validates a strong model for responsible large-scale data center development: securing substantial power capacity while ensuring that project-specific costs and risks are borne by the large-load customer, protecting existing ratepayers and creating incremental value for utilities and local communities. In its August 21, 2026 order, the Commission concluded: “After consideration of the entire record, the Commission finds that the proposed RESA contains adequate protections for existing customers, appropriately allocates financial and operational risks, establishes rates that are fair, just and reasonable, and provides for adequate and reliable service.” Under the approved structure, TeraWulf is responsible for the market, transmission, delivery and other costs attributable to serving its load, together with customer-specific infrastructure costs and substantial credit-support obligations.
[…]
The agreement also includes negotiated demand adders and customer charges that provide incremental contributions to Big Rivers Electric Corporation (“Big Rivers”) and Kenergy Corp.
[…]
The Justified Data Campus is being developed at the former Century Aluminum Hawesville facility, where approximately 482 MW of existing transmission capability remains available following the closure of the aluminum smelter.

sources.name: TeraWulf: Kentucky PSC approves Justified RESA
sources.excerpt:
TeraWulf Inc. (Nasdaq: WULF) (“TeraWulf” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated owner, developer and operator of large-scale digital infrastructure, today announced that the Kentucky Public Service Commission (“PSC”) has approved the Retail Electric Service Agreement (“RESA”) supporting up to 482 megawatts (“MW”) of electric service for TeraWulf’s Justified Data Campus in Hancock County, Kentucky. The approval represents an important milestone for Justified and, in TeraWulf’s view, validates a strong model for responsible large-scale data center development: securing substantial power capacity while ensuring that project-specific costs and risks are borne by the large-load customer, protecting existing ratepayers and creating incremental value for utilities and local communities. In its August 21, 2026 order, the Commission concluded: “After consideration of the entire record, the Commission finds that the proposed RESA contains adequate protections for existing customers, appropriately allocates financial and operational risks, establishes rates that are fair, just and reasonable, and provides for adequate and reliable service.” Under the approved structure, TeraWulf is responsible for the market, transmission, delivery and other costs attributable to serving its load, together with customer-specific infrastructure costs and substantial credit-support obligations.
[…]
The agreement also includes negotiated demand adders and customer charges that provide incremental contributions to Big Rivers Electric Corporation (“Big Rivers”) and Kenergy Corp.
[…]
The Justified Data Campus is being developed at the former Century Aluminum Hawesville facility, where approximately 482 MW of existing transmission capability remains available following the closure of the aluminum smelter.

sources.excerpt: Mount Pleasant datacenter project update Project overview Microsoft is developing a datacenter campus in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction update July 2026 As part of ongoing preparation at our datacenter site in Mount Pleasant, crews will begin moving soil materials between areas of the project site. Construction overview Starting on or around July 13, 2026, construction teams will begin hauling soil from one area of the site to another to support future development. This work is expected to continue for approximately eight weeks, depending on weather, permitting, and construction schedules. During this time, neighbors may notice: Increased truck traffic in and around the site. Movement of soil and construction materials. Stockpiling and early site preparation activity. Traffic and site operations Construction vehicles will use designated haul routes and approved access points within the project area. Teams will actively coordinate operations to help manage traffic flow and reduce impacts to the surrounding community. A map of the planned haul route is included for reference. Construction hours Construction activity will take place during permitted local construction hours. If work outside of these hours is required, it will follow all applicable local regulations. Staying connected We are committed to keeping our neighbors informed about construction activities. Questions about construction? Please contact Walsh Construction at MPDC@walshgroup.com or call 312-497-6967. Questions about other aspects of the project? Contact WisconsinDC@microsoft.com or leave a message at 608-535-3569. Learn more at local.microsoft.com/Wisconsin . June 2026: Community Connect Open House Microsoft hosted a Community Connect open house on June 23, 2026, at the Fountain Banquet Hall. The event provided an opportunity for community members to learn more about the Mount Pleasant datacenter project, hear the latest updates, and connect directly with subject matter experts. Attendees were able to ask questions and engage with project team members about ongoing construction activities, community investments, and upcoming milestones. Thank you to everyone who joined us and shared their feedback. Boards for Mount Pleasant Community Connect Open House April 2026: Community Office Hours Microsoft hosted “community office hours” for neighbors of the Mount Pleasant datacenter on April 9, 2026, at the Mount Pleasant Village Hall Ebe Auditorium. The informal session provided an opportunity for community members to hear about Mount Pleasant datacenter project updates, ask questions, and learn more about local investments and job opportunities. Thank you to everyone who participated. For those who were unable to attend, a link is available to view the presentation materials shared during the session. Boards for Mount Pleasant community office hours Construction update March 2026 Construction overview Construction continues at the Mount Pleasant Datacenter Campus , with progress underway across multiple phases. Phase 1—KR & 90th Work in this phase is nearing completion. Crews are finalizing interior work in several buildings and completing landscaping. Construction for Phase 1 is anticipated to be complete by spring 2026 . Phase 2—KR & H Construction activities for Phase 2 are ongoing and focused on expanding the site. Current work includes foundation installation, steel erection, and underground utility installation. This phase is scheduled to be completed in early 2028 . Phase 3—Durand & Hewitt Memorial Drive Preliminary earthwork is underway to prepare the site for future construction. To support construction operations, there are currently four site entrances: Gate 1: Highway KR Gate 2: Braun Road Gate 3: County Road H Gate 4: County Road H Construction schedule and activity Work is expected to begin in mid March , depending on ground conditions as seasonal thaw continues. To help reduce dust and debris on nearby roads, street sweepers will operate for approximately 10 hours per day . Tire wash systems are also in place at site exits to help keep surrounding roadways clean. Construction hours Construction activities are conducted in compliance with the Village of Mount Pleasant code. Work may take place between 6 AM and 10 PM, seven days per week . We appreciate your continued patience and cooperation as our crews move into the next phase of construction. Walsh Construction remains committed to minimizing disruption and maintaining safe, clean roadways throughout the project. Questions about construction? Contact Walsh Construction at MPDC@walshgroup.com . October 2025: Phase 2 construction update Microsoft is continuing development of the Mt. sources.name: Entergy Arkansas: Google West Memphis power service agreement
sources.excerpt:
Google is good for Arkansas
  and great for Entergy customers
  Google is investing $4 billion on cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure in
  Arkansas, including the development of a new data center in West Memphis
  – the company’s first facility in the state – powered by Entergy.
  Their historic investment in our state is bringing unparalleled benefits that will
  improve the lives of Arkansans for generations to come.


How will it benefit you?
           High tech partner = Lower cost power
           Google will cover the full energy costs associated with powering the facility, which will produce more
           than $1 billion in net customer savings over the life of the contract. In addition, as a new large industrial
           customer on our grid, Google will pick up more of the grid maintenance improvement costs that existing
           customers would otherwise have to bear alone and at a larger share than residential and small
           business customers.
           Adding any power-intensive facility to our grid can raise questions about its impact on service reliability
           for other customers, but we’ve ensured that our power service agreement with Google not only protects
           reliability for all customers, it improves it through measures such as:
           • Adding a new solar generation and battery storage facility in Jefferson County financially supported
             by Google.
           • Electrical infrastructure additions and improvements that will enhance reliability of the entire grid and
             lower costs for all customers.
           • A program to reduce data center power use during peak hours to support grid stability for all customers.

sources.excerpt: Today, OG&E, the operating subsidiary of locally-headquartered OGE Energy Corp. (NYSE: OGE), announced that it will power three new data centers that Google announced in Muskogee and Stillwater last year. The data centers and associated Electric Service Agreements will provide economic growth for local communities and the state, contribute to grid stability, and benefit OG&E's current customers. As technology continues to propel industry and our personal lives forward, OG&E will power the 21st century economy through these agreements with Google, whose data centers power key services that billions of people use every day, from online banking to hospital records to 911 systems. OG&E worked closely with Google to secure broad customer protections for years to come. Under this agreement, Google is committing to pay 100% of the costs to connect the data center sites to the grid as well as all contracted costs regardless of the company's energy use. Google will also pay its share of power generation required to serve these data centers. "OG&E is pleased to support Google and together advance growth in our home state, ensuring our current customers benefit from data center expansion that meets the technology needs of the 21st century economy at some of the lowest rates in the country," said Sean Trauschke, Chairman, President and CEO of OGE Energy Corp. "This unique agreement is a model for future data center partnerships and forms the basis for a new large-load The Electric Service Agreements and Capacity Purchase Agreements will be filed for review with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission in the coming days. The OCC must formally approve the agreement between OG&E and Google to supply power to the data center sites.            business customers.

           for other customers, but we’ve ensured that our power service agreement with Google not only protects
           reliability for all customers, it improves it through measures such as:

             by Google.
           • Electrical infrastructure additions and improvements that will enhance reliability of the entire grid and
             lower costs for all customers.
